mechanism_narrative: Sustained recovery in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES from their April troughs signals a durable return of commuting and workplace footfall, which spills over into retail-and-recreation trips and raises RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over the next 28 days is less than or equal to the last 28 days mean despite TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both improving from t-3w to t-0w.

mechanism_narrative: A WORKPLACES weekly mean crossing above -26.0 marks a regime shift from remote to office work, increasing daytime population and retail demand, so RETAIL_REC rises within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES weekly mean crosses above -26.0 from below
failure_condition: After WORKPLACES crosses above -26.0, RETAIL_REC over the following 14 days does not exceed the prior 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: The interaction of rising TRANSIT (less negative) and falling RESIDENTIAL (less positive) indicates a coordinated shift from staying home to out-of-home mobility, which lifts retail-and-recreation visits over four weeks.
failure_condition: When TRANSIT > -30.0 and RESIDENTIAL < 5.0, RETAIL_REC mean over the next 28 days is lower than over the last 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: In a post-omicron spring reopening regime, stable GROCERY_PHARM near -5 and positive PARKS signal reduced caution, allowing retail to recover over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: In the post-omicron reopening regime, RETAIL_REC fails to rise despite GROCERY_PHARM > -6.0 and PARKS > 0.

mechanism_narrative: A drop in RESIDENTIAL below 5.0 means fewer people are staying home all day, which directly increases discretionary retail-and-recreation trips over the next week.
failure_condition: After RESIDENTIAL falls below 5.0, RETAIL_REC in the following 7 days is not higher than the last 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: Spring seasonal warming raises PARKS visits above zero, and the associated outdoor activity increases overall retail-and-recreation footfall within one week.
failure_condition: When PARKS weekly mean is > 0, RETAIL_REC over the next 7 days does not rise relative to the last 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: The gap between improving WORKPLACES and still-depressed RETAIL_REC means retail has not yet fully captured the return-to-office wave, so retail will catch up over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over the next 28 days does not exceed the last 28 days mean despite WORKPLACES improving and RETAIL_REC lagging.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT remains below -30 for two consecutive weeks, capacity limits or residual restrictions keep retail suppressed, causing RETAIL_REC to decline over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT weekly mean < -30 for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: When TRANSIT stays below -30 for two consecutive weeks, RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days is higher than or equal to the last 28-day mean.
